3. Facts, in short, are that respondent No. 2- Southeast Bank Limited, Uttara Branch, Uttara Model Town, Dhaka (in short, the Bank), as plaintiff, on 21-10-2010 instituted Artha Rin Suit No. 153 of 2010 before the Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka (shortly, the Adalat) impleading the petitioner as defendant No. 4 (mortgagor and guarantor) and others for realization of outstanding loan amount of Taka 2,86,95,132.76 as on 30-9-2010 with interest till realization thereof (Annexure-A). The suit was decreed on contest by judgment and decree dated 27-11-2014 (decree signed on 1-12-2014) [Annexure-B and B-1]. The judgment debtors having failed to pay the decretal amount, the decree holder-Bank filed Artha Execution Case No. 51 of 2015 for recovery of the decretal amount (Annexure-C). During pendency of the execution case, the Bank preferred an application before the Adalat under section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (hereinafter referred to as the Ain, 2003) for issuance of certificate of possession and enjoyment of the mortgaged properties, which was allowed by the Adalat on 11-2-2016 and certificate was issued in favour of the Bank. Pursuant thereto, the Bank on 9-1-2017 without following the provision of section 6(5) of the Ain, 2003 preferred an application before the Adalat for taking over possession of schedule-1-A property of the petitioner. The Adalat by order dated 21-5-2017 allowed the application and issued writ of delivery of possession to that effect (Annexure-D and D-1). 

 11. He also submits that the principal borrower who is a Private Limited Company did not mortgage any property in favour of the Bank. The judgment-debtor No. 4-petitioner mortgaged his properties in favour of the Bank as a security to the loan. Since no property is mortgaged by the principal debtor, the property mortgaged to the Bank by the judgment-debtor No. 4 is to be sold in auction first and the decree would be transferred in favour of the mortgagor and he may execute the decree against the principal debtor in view of section 6(5) of the Ain, 2003. 

 13. Indisputably, Artha Rin Suit No. 153 of 2010 was initiated against the petitioner and others for realization of the defaulted loan amount, which was decreed on contest on 27-11-2014. The judgment-debtors having failed to pay the decretal amount the decree holder-Bank filed Artha Execution Case No. 51 of 2015 before the Adalat on 9-4-2015 to execute the decree. Notice of the execution case was duly served upon the petitioner but the same was returned as being not served and accordingly, the notice was published in the daily newspaper following the provision of section 30 of the Ain, 2003. Thereafter, the Adalat on the prayer of the Bank by order dated 7-9-2015 took initiative under section 33(1) of the Ain, 2003 to sell the mortgaged properties in auction. Pursuant thereto, the Bank published auction notices in 02 daily newspapers but no bidder participated in the auction process and, as such, the Adalat by order dated 14-10-2015 further fixed the next date on 1-11-2015 for step under section 33(4) of the Ain, 2003. Pursuant thereto, the Bank further published notices in 2 daily newspapers for auction sale of the mortgaged properties and accordingly, auction was held on 11-1-2016 but no bidder participated in the auction and thereby the procedure of section 33(1)(4) of the Ain, 2003 has been complied with. Thereafter, the Bank filed an application before the Adalat on 3-2-2016 under section 33(5) of the Ain, 2003 praying for issuance of certificate of possession and enjoyment in respect of the scheduled properties. After hearing the application, the Adalat by order dated 11-2-2016 rightly allowed the application, committing no illegality, holding that— 

 15. In the case in hand, the principal borrower, a private limited company, did not mortgage any property in favour of the Bank. But only the petitioner (judgment-debtor No. 4) mortgaged several properties in favour of the Bank as a security to the loan availed by the principal borrower. Since no property is mortgaged by the principal debtor, the properties mortgaged to the Bank by the judgment-debtor No. 4 is to be sold in auction first and the decree would be transferred in favour of the mortgagor and he may execute the decree against the principal debtor in view of section 6(5) of the Ain, 2003. 

 Our considered view is that if no property is mortgaged by the principal debtor in favour of the Bank as a security to the loan then firstly, the property mortgaged to the Bank by 3rd party mortgagor as a security to loan is to be sold in auction and the decree would be transferred in favour of the 3rd party mortgagor and he may execute the decree against the principal debtor in view of the provision of section 6(5) of the Ain."
